newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures whittle gains after U.S. ECI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures whittle gains after U.S. ECI.

text.p: July 29 - U.S. debt futures firmed at the outset and then barely whittled gains after Q2 US employment cost index that matched forecasts for a 0.8-pct rise. The Q1 ECI remained at up 0.6 pct. Sept T-bonds briefly probed above the 115-23/32 recent high. Support also from ideas are on verge of US balanced budget pact.
The market also faces July U.S. consumer confidence, seen firming to 130.4, at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT.

Futures already had gained support in late pit trading Monday from news the White House and Congressional Republicans were on the verge of reaching a balanced budget pact. Early Tuesday, White House budget director Franklin Raines predicted that the budget deal hammered out Monday will pass Congress.
Despite the slight futures pullback early Tuesday, brokers said the market still remained tilted to the upside.
"We had some size selling, long liquidation," said a third broker of the erosion. "Other than that, it still looks good."
"Even in a correction, you're only down a couple ticks," added the broker. "It's (pullback) not awful."

He called 115-08/32 pivotal, adding that a fall below there could trigger more long liquidation. On the upside, he pegged first intraday resistance at 115-29/32, with a rise above there seen fostering a move toward 116-07/32.

At 0829 CDT/1329 GMT, September T-bonds were flat at 115-14/32, T-notes rose 2/32 to 110-08/32, muni-bonds lost 4/32 to 115-14/32, December Eurodollars rose 0.005 to 94.145, and September T-bills added 0.005 to 94.910. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750))
